Name: In-process LRU cache (Caffeine/Guava/Ristretto/lru-cache)
Use Case: Hot config, tiny lookups, request-scoped memoisation
Weaknesses: No cross-instance coherence; doubles memory per replica
Pitfalls: Stale data after writes; size sprawl
Notes: Caffeine is the gold standard on JVM (W-TinyLFU); Ristretto on Go.

Name: Redis cache (single + replica)
Use Case: Session store, cached query results, rate-limit, distributed locks
Strengths: Sub-ms over network, rich data types, ubiquitous tooling
Weaknesses: Memory cost; cluster mode has multi-key constraints
Pitfalls: Hot keys on single shard; expiry-driven stampedes
Notes: Use 'EXPIRE' with jitter and 'SET NX EX' for distributed locks (with caution).

Name: Redis Cluster
Weaknesses: Multi-key ops require hash tags; cross-slot transactions impossible
Pitfalls: Bad hash tag design causes hot shards
Notes: Co-locate related keys with hash tags '{user:42}:profile'.

Name: CDN edge cache (Cloudflare/Fastly/CloudFront/Akamai)
Use Case: Static assets, public JSON APIs, image transforms
Strengths: Drops origin load 90%+; lowest latency to user
Weaknesses: Invalidation latency; cache-key design errors leak data between users
Notes: Always set 'Vary' / 'Cache-Control' explicitly; never rely on defaults for auth'd routes.

Name: HTTP cache (Cache-Control + ETag)
Use Case: Public APIs, static assets, conditional GETs

Name: Read-through (CDN / Hazelcast / Apollo)"
Weaknesses: Coupled to cache library; thundering herd risk
Pitfalls: Concurrent miss → many origin calls; need request coalescing
Notes: Always wrap loaders with single-flight / coalescing to avoid stampedes.

Name: Write-through cache
Use Case: Datasets where reads dominate but writes must be visible immediately
Weaknesses: Doubles write latency; both stores must be available
Pitfalls: Partial failure inconsistency; treat as transactional outbox
Notes: Combine with idempotency to handle partial-failure retries.

Name: Write-back / write-behind cache
Use Case: High-throughput writes where loss of last seconds is acceptable
Weaknesses: Risk of data loss on crash; complex recovery
Notes: Pair with WAL / persistent queue if data loss is unacceptable.

Name: Negative caching
Strengths: Prevents repeated expensive lookups for non-existent keys
Weaknesses: Risk of caching a transient miss as permanent

Name: Bloom filter / Cuckoo filter
Use Case: Avoid expensive lookups for definitely-missing keys (e.g., DB row exists)
Pitfalls: Sizing for target FPR; resizing requires rebuild
Notes: RedisBloom & many DBs (Cassandra) ship one. Tune FPR to ~1%.

Name: L1+L2 hybrid (in-process + Redis)
Use Case: Reduce Redis QPS while keeping cross-instance coherence (mostly)
Strengths: Best price/perf; 99% in-process hit rate possible
Weaknesses: Stale L1 after invalidations; coherence is 'soft'
Pitfalls: Use Pub/Sub or short L1 TTL to bound staleness
Notes: Common pattern: 60s L1 TTL + Redis pub/sub busts on writes.
